title: Saga patterns with Step Functions (compensation and rollback)
hook: A saga coordinates a distributed transaction as a sequence of local steps with compensating actions on failure. AWS Step Functions Catch blocks route to rollback Tasks — the pattern behind order, payment, and inventory workflows in senior system design interviews.

blocks.text: Choreography saga: each service listens and reacts — no central coordinator. Orchestration saga: Step Functions state machine calls each service in order and runs compensators (refund, release inventory) when a later step fails. Compensators must be idempotent — they may run more than once on retry.

entries.plainDefinition: Sequence of local transactions with compensating undo steps.
entries.example: Reserve → Charge → Ship; on ship fail → Refund → Release.

entries.plainDefinition: Semantic undo of a completed forward step.
Central coordinator drives steps and compensation.
entries.example: Step Functions state machine owns flow.

entries.plainDefinition: Services react to events without central brain.
entries.example: SNS events trigger each compensator independently.

blocks.text: Two-phase commit across microservices does not scale on AWS. Sagas accept eventual consistency with explicit rollback. Interview gold: distinguish retryable Lambda.ServiceException (Retry block) from business failure ShipFailed (Catch to compensator). Missing idempotent refund causes double refund on compensator retry.

blocks.title: Interview framing
blocks.body: Say: forward steps sequential; Catch routes to compensators in reverse order; compensators idempotent; Step Functions Standard for audit.

blocks.title: Pitfalls to avoid
blocks.body: Retry on PaymentDeclined — infinite loop. Compensator without idempotency — double refund. Catch States.ALL masking bugs. Choreography when audit requires single execution record.

blocks.text: How to prove it in production: integration test inject ShipFailed — verify Refund and Release in history. Alarm on compensator Fail state. Pair with aws-12-sqs-idempotency patterns for worker-side dedup. Saga vs 2PC: sagas accept temporary inconsistency visible to users — document UX.

blocks.title: What gets you rejected in interviews
blocks.body: Saying 'rollback is just DELETE FROM orders.' Strong answer: semantic compensators (refund API, release reservation) that are idempotent and may leave audit records.

interviewTakeaways: Saga = forward steps + compensating undo on failure; orchestration via Step Functions Catch blocks.
Retry transient errors only; business failures route to compensators.
Compensators must be idempotent — Step Functions may retry them.
60s: Reserve charge ship. Ship fail Catch to refund release. Idempotent compensators. Standard for audit.
Follow-up: choreography saga with EventBridge versus orchestration?
commonPitfalls: Retry on business decline — infinite charge attempts.
Strong answer: Catch PaymentDeclined → ReleaseInventory without Retry.
Using Express for saga needing multi-day human approval.
